title: CVE-2026-94266: password leak in CURLINFO_EFFECTIVE_URL
excerpt:
A `.netrc`-sourced password, injected into the live URL handle at login time, survives an ordinary same-host relative `Location:` redirect and ends up verbatim in `data->state.url`, so it is exposed via `CURLINFO_EFFECTIVE_URL`, `curl -w '%{url_effective}'`, and verbose (`-v`) output.

## Affected code

https://github.com/curl/curl/blob/d1823ebc17e5778c30f8a6b2221a057ec607a9b7/lib/url.c#L1325-L1332

```c
      result = Curl_creds_merge(ncreds_out->user, ncreds_out->passwd,
                                *pcreds, CREDS_NETRC, pcreds);
      if(result)
        goto out;
      /* for updated strings, we update them in the URL */
      uc = curl_url_set(data->state.uh, CURLUPART_USER,
                        Curl_creds_user(*pcreds), CURLU_URLENCODE);
      if(!uc)
        uc = curl_url_set(data->state.uh, CURLUPART_PASSWORD,
                          Curl_creds_passwd(*pcreds),
                          CURLU_URLENCODE);
```

https://github.com/curl/curl/blob/d1823ebc17e5778c30f8a6b2221a057ec607a9b7/lib/http.c#L1244

https://github.com/curl/curl/blob/d1823ebc17e5778c30f8a6b2221a057ec607a9b7/lib/http.c#L1298-L1306

https://github.com/curl/curl/blob/d1823ebc17e5778c30f8a6b2221a057ec607a9b7/lib/urlapi.c#L1334-L1401

https://github.com/curl/curl/blob/d1823ebc17e5778c30f8a6b2221a057ec607a9b7/lib/getinfo.c#L83-L86

## Details

1. `url_set_data_creds_netrc()` (lib/url.c:1325-1332) writes the `.netrc` user/password directly into `data->state.uh`, the handle later reused to compute the effective URL. It is never cleared.
2. On a redirect, `Curl_http_follow()` calls `curl_url_set(data->state.uh, CURLUPART_URL, newurl, ...)` (http.c:1244), reparsing the same, already-dirty handle with the `Location:` value.
3. For a relative `Location: /path`, `redirect_url()` (urlapi.c:1334) computes `cutoff = strchr(protsep, '/')` and copies `base[0..cutoff)`, i.e. `scheme://user:pass@host:port`, verbatim into the new URL before appending the new path (urlapi.c:1355-1362, 1391-1397). `CURLU_URLENCODE` only percent-escapes non-unreserved bytes, so a plain alphanumeric password passes through unchanged.
4. The result is read back and stored: `Curl_bufref_set(&data->state.url, follow_url, ...)` (http.c:1298) and `infof(data, "Issue another request to this URL: '%s'", follow_url)` (http.c:1306).
5. `CURLINFO_EFFECTIVE_URL` returns `Curl_bufref_ptr(&data->state.url)` unsanitized (getinfo.c:

claims.reasoning: The follow_url containing the netrc credentials is stored in data->state.url and directly returned by CURLINFO_EFFECTIVE_URL. The same string is printed by infof (verbose/debug output) and is available via the %{url_effective} write-out variable.

claims.text: Using a .netrc with a password and a server that responds with a relative Location:, curl -v -L --netrc-file netrc_test --netrc-optional -w '\nEFFECTIVE_URL=%{url_effective}\n' http://127.0.0.1:25036/first reproduces the leak.

key_reasons: The code confirms .netrc credentials are written into data->state.uh and never cleared (lib/url.c:1327-1332).
Redirect processing reuses the same handle (lib/http.c:1244).
For relative redirects, redirect_url copies the authority including userinfo into the new URL (lib/urlapi.c:1364,1392,1397).
The resulting URL is stored in data->state.url and exposed via CURLINFO_EFFECTIVE_URL, verbose output, and write-out variables (lib/http.c:1304,1306; lib/getinfo.c:84).
Absolute redirects do not leak because set_url calls parseurl_and_replace which fully replaces the handle (lib/urlapi.c:1855), but the relative path does not.
The project policy does not classify this confidentiality flaw as a non-security issue.
reply: Thank you for the detailed report and reproduction. The code confirms the flaw: url_set_data_creds_netrc injects credentials into data->state.uh (lib/url.c:1327-1332), the redirect logic reuses that handle (lib/http.c:1244), and for relative Location: headers, redirect_url copies the userinfo into the new URL (lib/urlapi.c:1364,1392,1397). The result reaches CURLINFO_EFFECTIVE_URL, verbose logs, and %{url_effective} (lib/http.c:1304,1306; lib/getinfo.c:84). This is a valid confidentiality issue. The fix should strip userinfo from the handle before computing the redirect URL, as the Referer builder does (lib/http.c:1219-1221) and the proxy target builder does (lib/http.c:2163-2172).
